item.title: Archive
item.description:
Mojo struct 🡭

Archive

@memory_only
struct Archive

Reads entry metadata and contents from an in-memory ZIP archive.

Opening an archive copies the input span into native-owned storage, so the caller may release or reuse the original bytes afterward. Entry indexes are zero-based and remain valid for the lifetime of the archive.

Examples:

var archive = Archive(Span(archive_data))
print("entries:", archive.len())
for raw_index in range(Int(archive.len())):
 var entry = archive.entry(UInt(raw_index))
 print(entry.name(), entry.size())

Implemented traits

AnyType, Deinitable, Movable

Methods

➕  ➖

__init__ 

def __init__(out self, data: Span[UInt8])

Opens a ZIP archive from an in-memory byte span. Args:

  • data (Span[UInt8]): The complete encoded ZIP archive. The bytes are copied.
  • self (Self)

Returns:

Self

Raises:

An error if the data is not a valid or supported ZIP archive.

open 

@staticmethod
def open(data: Span[UInt8]) -> Self

Opens a ZIP archive from an in-memory byte span. This named constructor is equivalent to Archive(data).

Args:

  • data (Span[UInt8]): The complete encoded ZIP archive. The bytes are copied.

Returns:

Self: The opened archive.

Raises:

An error if the data is not a valid or supported ZIP archive.

len 

def len(self) -> UInt

Returns the number of entries in the archive. Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

UInt: The number of file and directory entries.

Raises:

An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.

is_empty 

def is_empty(self) -> Bool

Checks whether the archive contains no entries. Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

Bool: True when Archive.len is zero, otherwise False.

Raises:

An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.

index_for_name 

def index_for_name(self, name: String) -> Optional[UInt]

Looks up an entry index by its exact stored name. Names are case-sensitive and use the separators stored in the archive.

Examples:

var maybe_index = archive.index_for_name("docs/readme.txt")
if maybe_index:
 print("entry index:", maybe_index.value())

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • name (String): The exact entry name to find.

Returns:

Optional[UInt]: The zero-based index when present, otherwise None.

Raises:

An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.

entry 

def entry(mut self, index: UInt) -> Entry

Returns an immutable metadata snapshot for one entry. Args:

  • self (Self)
  • index (UInt): A zero-based index smaller than Archive.len.

Returns:

Entry: Metadata including the name, sizes, CRC-32, compression method, file kind, and optional Unix mode.

Raises:

An error if the index is out of range or the native archive is invalid.

read_entry 

def read_entry(mut self, index: UInt) -> ZipBytes

Decompresses an entry into a newly allocated byte buffer. Directory entries normally produce an empty buffer. For caller-provided storage, use Archive.read_into instead.

Examples:

var index = archive.index_for_name("hello.txt").value()
var bytes = archive.read_entry(index).to_list()
print(String(from_utf8=Span(bytes)))

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • index (UInt): A zero-based index smaller than Archive.len.

Returns:

ZipBytes: The complete uncompressed entry contents.

Raises:

An error if the index is out of range, the entry cannot be decompressed, memory cannot be reserved, or the native archive is invalid.

read_into 

def read_into(mut self, index: UInt, buffer: Span[UInt8]) -> UInt

Decompresses an entry into an exact-size caller-provided buffer. The destination length must equal Entry.size() for the selected entry. No partial reads are performed.

Examples:

var entry = archive.entry(index)
var destination = List[UInt8](unsafe_uninit_length=Int(entry.size()))
var written = archive.read_into(index, Span(destination))

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • index (UInt): A zero-based index smaller than Archive.len.
  • buffer (Span[UInt8]): A mutable destination whose length exactly matches the uncompressed entry size.

Returns:

UInt: The number of bytes written, equal to len(buffer) on success.

Raises:

An error if the index is invalid, the destination has the wrong length, decompression fails, or the native archive is invalid.

comment 

def comment(self) -> ZipBytes

Returns the archive-level comment as raw bytes. ZIP comments are not required to be UTF-8. Convert the returned bytes to String only when the archive’s encoding is known.

Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

ZipBytes: The archive comment, or an empty buffer when no comment is present.

Raises:

An error if the underlying native archive is no longer valid.

item.title: ZipBytes
item.description:
Mojo struct 🡭

ZipBytes

@memory_only
struct ZipBytes

Owns a byte buffer returned by the Rust ZIP implementation.

ZipBytes values contain either a completed archive from ZipWriter.finish, entry contents from Archive.read_entry, or an archive comment from Archive.comment. Copy the bytes into Mojo-owned storage with ZipBytes.to_list or into an existing destination with ZipBytes.fill.

Implemented traits

AnyType, Deinitable, Movable

Methods

➕  ➖

len 

def len(self) -> UInt

Returns the number of bytes in the buffer. Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

UInt: The buffer length in bytes.

Raises:

An error if the underlying native value is no longer valid.

fill 

def fill(self, buffer: Span[UInt8]) -> UInt

Copies bytes into an existing mutable span. At most len(buffer) bytes are copied. Use a destination of ZipBytes.len bytes to copy the entire value.

Examples:

var destination = List[UInt8](unsafe_uninit_length=Int(contents.len()))
var copied = contents.fill(Span(destination))

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • buffer (Span[UInt8]): The destination span to fill.

Returns:

UInt: The number of bytes copied.

Raises:

An error if the underlying native value is no longer valid.

to_list 

def to_list(self) -> List[UInt8]

Copies the complete buffer into a new Mojo List[UInt8]. Examples:

var bytes = contents.to_list()
var text = String(from_utf8=Span(bytes))

Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

List[UInt8]: A newly allocated list containing every byte.

Raises:

An error if the native value is invalid or the native copy reports an unexpected length.

item.title: ZipWriter
item.description:
Mojo struct 🡭

ZipWriter

@memory_only
struct ZipWriter

Builds a ZIP archive entirely in memory.

Add files and directories, optionally set an archive comment, then call ZipWriter.finish exactly once. Stored and Deflate compression are supported. A finished writer rejects further mutations.

Examples:

var writer = ZipWriter()
writer.add_directory("docs/")
writer.add_file(
 "docs/hello.txt",
 "hello from Mojo".as_bytes(),
 Compression_Deflated,
)
writer.set_comment("created by ziprs")
var archive_bytes = writer.finish()

Implemented traits

AnyType, Deinitable, Movable

Methods

➕  ➖

__init__ 

def __init__(out self)

Creates an empty in-memory ZIP writer. Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

Self

Raises:

An error if the native writer cannot be initialized.

is_finished 

def is_finished(self) -> Bool

Checks whether ZipWriter.finish has already consumed the writer output. Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

Bool: True after a successful call to ZipWriter.finish, otherwise False.

Raises:

An error if the underlying native writer is no longer valid.

add_file 

def add_file(mut self, name: String, data: Span[UInt8], compression: Int32 = Int32(1))

Adds one file entry and copies its data into the archive. Examples:

var payload = String("important data")
writer.add_file("data.txt", payload.as_bytes(), Compression_Stored)

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • name (String): The path stored in the ZIP directory, conventionally using / separators.
  • data (Span[UInt8]): The uncompressed file contents.
  • compression (Int32): Compression_Deflated by default, or Compression_Stored.

Raises:

An error if the writer is finished, the compression value is unsupported, or the entry cannot be written.

add_directory 

def add_directory(mut self, name: String)

Adds an explicit directory entry. Examples:

writer.add_directory("images/")

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • name (String): The directory path to store. A trailing / is recommended.

Raises:

An error if the writer is finished or the directory entry cannot be written.

set_comment 

def set_comment(mut self, comment: String)

Sets the archive-level UTF-8 comment. Calling this method again replaces the previous comment.

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • comment (String): The comment text to store.

Raises:

An error if the writer is finished or the comment cannot be stored.

finish 

def finish(mut self) -> ZipBytes

Finalizes the central directory and returns the encoded archive. This method succeeds only once. Use ZipWriter.is_finished to query the writer state.

Examples:

var archive_bytes = writer.finish()
var storage = archive_bytes.to_list()
with open("example.zip", "w") as output:
 output.write_bytes(Span(storage))

Args:

  • self (Self)

Returns:

ZipBytes: The complete encoded ZIP archive.

Raises:

An error if the writer was already finished or finalization fails.
